newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt backs down on doctor night fee cuts.
newsitem.headline: French govt backs down on doctor night fee cuts.

text.p: The French government has decided not to back a plan to cut the hours in which doctors can charge higher night fees, a decision some called a climb-down from efforts to reform France's health care system.

"The Prime Minister confirmed...that the government does not approve a reduction in night tariffs for doctors and that it would not pursue the proposal from the CNAM (national health insurance fund)," RPR political party head Michel Pericard told reporters after meeting Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Tuesday.
Currency analysts voiced concern about the climb-down, which follows strenuous efforts by European governments to cut budget deficits to qualify for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"Fundamentally, signs that Juppe is backing away from some healthcare proposals may encourage other groups to press for concessions," said Nick Parsons, forex strategist at Banque Paribas in Paris.
The franc was trading at 3.3802/07 per mark by 1020 GMT, down from late Tuesday's European level of 3.3771/75.

This is the second time in two months the French government has rowed back on proposed reforms to the heavily indebted health care system and prompted a member of the pro-reform CFDT union, which heads the CNAM, to question the government's commitment to reform.

"If each time the health professions rush to the ramparts the government backs down, it speaks badly of its will to put in place the whole range of medical savings and sanctions for unscrupulous doctors," daily Liberation quoted a CFDT source as saying.
In September the government put on indefinite hold a plan to cut the use of ambulances after drivers staged work slowdowns and protest marches in cities around France.
Doctors in France have to right to raise their fees from 8 PM at night until 7 AM in the morning. The reform would have pushed back night fee hours to 9 PM.
The two abandoned reforms were part of a 4.2 billion franc package of savings proposed by the CNAM aimed at cutting the deficit of the health system's deficit.
Preliminary estimates put the health care system's deficit at about 33 billion francs in 1996. The night tariff cuts would have saved about 103 million francs next year.
